statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band and well below the block threshold, while Stress stays elevated on an unresolved Gulf conflict, Brent above $90 and the 10-year Treasury yield at its highest level since January 2025.
recommendation: Conditions are described as ordinary but macro-stressed. A narrow evidence-based caution window is mapped around the 13:30 UTC US cash open and the 14:00 UTC ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS cluster, where the forecast policy state steps to WATCH for two hours before returning to EA_ON.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a 44-point overnight range while oil, long-end yields and the Gulf escalation carry the macro stress
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed 31 August at 29,456.97, up 0.08% inside a narrow 29,304.49-29,483.90 session range, outperforming the S&P 500 (-0.33%) and the Dow (-0.70%) and finishing August 3.8% higher. NQ futures are near 29,509.75 with a Globex range of roughly 29,478-29,523, a two-sided span of about 44 points that shows no directional efficiency, and VIX is 14.92. The macro backdrop is materially more stressed than the price path. US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island, Iran attacked US positions in Jordan and the UAE, and threats have been extended to the Kharg Island export hub, leaving Brent near $91.15 and WTI near $86.61. The 10-year Treasury yield is about 4.78% and the 30-year about 5.26%, with September rate-hike pricing near 62% after the Jackson Hole address. Asian equities are lower, with the Nikkei 225 off about 0.91% and the Kospi down more than 1%, yet US index futures are flat and the latest-session internals show semiconductors firm against weaker megacap software rather than a single directional impulse. That cross-asset conflict raises Stress rather than Tail: none of the shallow-pullback, failed-retracement or session-extreme behaviour that defines a pathological price path has been observed. Scheduled ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS data at 14:00 UTC, followed by ADP, ISM Services and the 4 September payrolls report, are treated as checkpoints rather than as observed evidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Tail stayed between 5 and 17 across 31 August with the policy state mapped to EA_ON in every hour. Stress rose from the high-30s during the Asian session to the low-to-mid 50s once the Gulf escalation, the oil move and the long-end yield rise were absorbed through European and US hours, then eased to about 50 into the overnight session. Dominant mode was mixed apart from a short event/whipsaw phase around 09:00-10:00 UTC, and confidence held between 84 and 88.
outlookSummary: The base case is a continuation of ordinary, two-sided conditions through the remaining Asian and European hours, with conditional Tail easing to 8 in the quietest windows. Risk concentrates on the 13:00-15:00 UTC block covering the Fed Barr remarks, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS cluster, where forecast Tail peaks at 21 and the mapped policy state steps to WATCH for two hours before decaying back into the low band through the US afternoon. Stress stays in the low-to-high fifties across the whole horizon because oil above $90 Brent, the long end of the Treasury curve, September rate-hike pricing and the unresolved Strait of Hormuz situation all remain live, and the week's dominant checkpoint, the 4 September payrolls report, sits beyond this window.
